# Fiddle leaf fig leaf drop

## What happened

The Ficus lyrata (a retirement present from the staff at Moretonhampstead Primary, July 2020) was 1.6 m tall and perfectly happy in the conservatory. On 2 November 2024 I moved it into the sitting room for the winter because the conservatory gets down to 4°C at night. Between 9 and 23 November it dropped seven leaves, all from the lower half, each one with a brown patch at the edge first and then simply letting go.

## Suspects

### Light

Borrowed Derek Yeo's lux meter. Conservatory in November at midday: 3,200 lux. The sitting room spot by the bookcase: 900 lux. That alone would do it.

### Draught

It was a metre from the door to the hall. Every time the door opened, cold air. I hadn't thought of it.

### The radiator

Directly under the window next to it. Colin bled the radiators on 1 November (see [[Bleeding radiators]]), after which they ran properly hot for the first time in years. Leaves on the radiator side were the crispy ones.

### Water

Probably not. I'd kept to the fortnightly drink in [[Watering schedule]] and checked with a chopstick.

## What I changed

- 25 November: moved to the south bay window, away from the radiator, 2.1 m from the door
- Put a cheap thermometer next to it: 15 to 19°C, steady
- Turned it a quarter turn every Sunday
- Topped up light with the panel from [[Grow light buying notes]] for a few weeks over Christmas, 4 pm to 9 pm

## Result

Two more leaves dropped in early December, then it stopped. New bud at the top on 3 March 2025. Lesson: these figs hate being moved more than anything. One spot, and leave it there.
